title: First constraints on the nonperturbative gluon Collins-Soper kernel
summary: The gluon Collins-Soper kernel, which encodes the rapidity evolution of transverse-momentum-dependent gluon distributions, is constrained for the first time in the nonperturbative regime, for transverse momentum scales $q_{T} \in [ 300\text{ MeV}, 1.3\text{ GeV}]$. The constraints are determined in lattice QCD at a close-to-physical pion mass $M_π= 172(3)\text{ MeV}$, a single lattice spacing $a=0.15\text{ fm}$, and next-to-next-to-leading logarithmic matching in Large-Momentum Effective Theory. These results represent the first step toward a controlled determination of the gluon Collins-Soper kernel in QCD, with eventual phenomenological import and relevance to present and future experiments sensitive to the gluon structure of hadronic matter.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the first constraints on the gluon Collins-Soper kernel, a function that describes the rapidity evolution of transverse-momentum-dependent gluon distributions, in a nonperturbative regime. The study uses lattice QCD simulations and is significant for understanding the gluon structure of hadronic matter, with potential implications for current and future experiments.
AI.motivation: The motivation behind this work is to provide a controlled determination of the gluon Collins-Soper kernel, which is essential for understanding the gluon structure within hadrons. This knowledge is important for the interpretation of experimental data from particle physics experiments that are sensitive to the behavior of gluons at different momentum scales.
AI.method: The researchers use lattice Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) to calculate the gluon Collins-Soper kernel. The simulation is carried out at a pion mass close to its physical value, a specific lattice spacing, and incorporates next-to-next-to-leading logarithmic matching within the framework of Large-Momentum Effective Theory (LaMET).
AI.result: The results yield the first set of constraints on the gluon Collins-Soper kernel in the nonperturbative region, specifically for transverse momentum scales between 300 MeV and 1.3 GeV. These findings pave the way for more accurate predictions of gluon distribution functions, which are necessary for high-energy collider phenomenology.
AI.conclusion: The conclusion drawn from this research is that it represents a significant step towards a better understanding of the gluon structure of hadronic matter. The constrained gluon Collins-Soper kernel will be of importance for both existing and upcoming experiments, as it will allow for more precise theoretical calculations and interpretations of experimental data.

title: Analytic decomposition of two-body electroweak processes with left-hand cuts
summary: We derive an on-shell representation for electroweak $2+J\to2$ transition amplitudes involving two hadrons in both the initial and final state for systems where there are left-hand singularities generated by light-particle exchange, e.g. one-pion exchange. The derivation treats the insertion of the electroweak current perturbatively, keeping only the leading-order contribution in the external field, while the hadronic interactions are treated to all orders, including one-particle exchange effects. We find that, in such processes, the amplitude can have logarithmic singularities, as well as one-particle pole singularities, due to these exchanges. We isolate those contributions, as well as previously identified triangle singularities. The result is expressed in terms of the purely hadronic amplitude, exchange-current kernels, triangle functions, and a class of short-distance transition functions that are real and smooth below unaccounted-for thresholds. While we consider only transitions with spinless particles, this work is an important step toward constraining form factors of systems involving nucleons or vector mesons in the heavy quark sector, where the one-pion-exchange singularity is quite close to threshold.

AI.tldr: The paper presents an on-shell representation for electroweak 2+J to 2 transition amplitudes, with a focus on systems involving light-particle exchanges, and identifies the presence of logarithmic and one-particle pole singularities. It also contributes to the understanding of form factors in heavy quark sectors.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to derive an on-shell representation for electroweak transition amplitudes that involve hadrons, considering the effects of light-particle exchange, such as one-pion exchange, and to identify singularities due to these exchanges, which is important for constraining form factors in systems with nucleons or vector mesons.
AI.method: The method involves a perturbative treatment of the electroweak current insertion, keeping only the leading-order contribution, while hadronic interactions are treated to all orders including one-particle exchange effects. The analysis isolates contributions from logarithmic and one-particle pole singularities, as well as triangle singularities.
AI.result: The result is an expression for the amplitude in terms of hadronic amplitudes, exchange-current kernels, triangle functions, and short-distance transition functions, which are real and smooth below certain thresholds.
